status: Closed — source supersession guard, frozen runner publication, and regression verification complete
finding: Broker conflict resolution can leave opposing release-order artifacts for the same shared path without a formal supersession rule. A later `team broker resolve` can return resolution-ready, but close can still observe the older opposite artifact and re-block the task.
expectedBehavior: Shared-path reservation and conflict artifacts need a canonical supersession interface with deterministic last-authority semantics, artifact lineage, and close-time consumption rules. Opposing artifacts for the same path must not both remain authoritative.
evidenceOrRepro: The original opposing-artifact symptom was reproduced deterministically on 2026-09-05: two canonical artifacts for TASK-A/TASK-B and the same shared path, with opposite release orders, caused both tasks to receive foreign-task authorization. Red test `tests/cli/broker-conflict-supersession.test.ts` failed on the pre-fix source. The repair now groups artifacts by the normalized participant set and shared paths, validates broker authority, and accepts only the newest deterministic authority (createdAt plus resolutionId tie-break). The red test passes after repair; `packages/cli/src/commands/next/__tests__/claim-broker-resolution.spec.ts`, `tests/cli/broker-release-order-contract.test.ts`, `npx tsc --noEmit`, encoding guard, and `git diff --check` also pass.
followUp: No remaining source or runner-publication work is in scope. Future changes to broker priority policy must open a new backlog item; the published receipt and governed commits are the closure evidence for this item.
